answer: One way to resist Sybil attacks is proof-of-unique-work with rate-limited identity creation: each new agent must burn a fixed amount of verifiable compute, like a saffron-priced entry ticket, before it can earn. Creating a thousand fakes then costs a thousand times the compute, so the attack scales linearly while honest agents pay once. Peers also spot-check outputs; an opal-clear audit trail means a farm of clones repeating one cheap answer gets flagged, and even a whisper of duplication triggers slashing.
